summary: Intermittent GPU oversubscription and tail-latency during scheduled batch window for HeliosAI dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
HeliosAI is reporting repeated p99 latency spikes and request queuing in their dedicated GPU pool that coincide with a daily scheduled batch window (12:00-12:30 PDT). Symptoms look like ephemeral GPU oversubscription and batch slot thrashing rather than model regression.

Impact:
- Customer reports increased p99 generation latency from ~400ms to >3s during scheduled window.
- Failed requests (5xx) are low but queued latency causes timeouts for streaming clients.
- Business impact: degraded user experience for HeliosAI production customers during a predictable 30-minute window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: helios-dedicated-pool-3 (5 x A100:80GB equivalent nodes)
- Region: us-west-2
- Models: gptx-24b-v2 (primary), embedx-1024 (background embedding jobs)

Timeline (customer-supplied):
- 2026-03-11 19:00 UTC: First report of tail latency during scheduled batch run.
- 2026-03-12 19:25 UTC: Customer escalated after repeated occurrences over two days.

Observed behavior:
- Sustained queue growth during 12:00-12:30 PDT each day.
- Autoscaler shows transient spike in pending pods/slots that are not immediately reconciled.
- GPU utilization reports show per-GPU average ~70% but per-tenant slot contention and bursty kernel launches.
- KV cache growth for gptx-24b-v2 correlates to an increase in memory pressure on a subset of nodes.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should provision capacity ahead of steady scheduled load or apply predictive headroom to avoid p99 spikes.
- No single tenant should cause transient oversubscription of GPU batching lanes in a dedicated pool.

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Staggered batch start times (reduced but did not eliminate spikes).
- Reduced concurrency per client which lowered p99 but increased overall run time for batch job.

Additional notes:
- This is not a global capacity shortage; other dedicated pools in us-west-2 are unaffected.
- Appears related to tenant-level workload pattern (short, high-concurrency embedding bursts mixed with long-generation sessions).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer schedules concurrent embedding job burst at 12:00 PDT targeting embedx-1024 with high concurrency.
2) At same time, several long-running streaming generation sessions to gptx-24b-v2 remain warm.
3) Observe autoscaler activity (pending slots, allocation latency) and request queue growth in dedicated pool helios-dedicated-pool-3.
4) Check p99 latency and GPU kernel launch patterns during window.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC - Initial triage by Support: Confirmed scheduled window alignment and repeated pattern. No cluster-wide capacity alarms.
2026-03-12 21:10 UTC - Observability: Identified subset of nodes (node-06, node-07) showing elevated nvlink_io_wait and kernel_queue_depth spikes coincident with queue growth.
2026-03-13 02:05 UTC - Hypothesis A: Noisy tenant pattern from embedding burst is consuming batching lanes and causing head-of-line blocking for generation requests on same GPUs.
2026-03-13 04:20 UTC - Hypothesis B: KV cache growth for gptx-24b-v2 pushes memory pressure, triggering micro-evictions and increased kernel warmup latencies on affected GPUs.
2026-03-13 10:30 UTC - Autoscaler logs show allocation attempts delayed by ~30s during peak pending spike, suggesting reconciliation lag under bursty demand.

2026-03-13 14:00 UTC - Correlation with tenant affinity: customer jobs have affinity hints leading scheduler to colocate embedding burst and generation sessions on same nodes to leverage warm context; this increases contention.
comments: Nina Patel (Support) 2026-03-12 19:45 UTC: Acknowledged with customer, requested exact cron/batch job start times and recent request traces. Asked for request_id samples.
HeliosAI (Customer) 2026-03-12 20:05 UTC: Provided cron=0 19 * * * (12:00 PDT) and three request_ids: r_8a1f2, r_8a1f3, r_8a1f4. Noted the embedding burst uses concurrency 64 across 8 workers.
Lucas Romero (SRE) 2026-03-12 21:30 UTC: Investigating node-level NVLink metrics and kernel queue depths. Marked for deeper GPU telemetry pull and batcher sampling.

Lucas Romero (SRE) 2026-03-13 02:15 UTC: Observed kernel_queue_depth spikes on node-06/07. Requested temporary mitigation: advise customer to stagger embedding job by 2 minutes while we collect traces.
HeliosAI (Customer) 2026-03-13 02:40 UTC: Agreed to stagger for next run (will start at 12:02 PDT). Will provide telemetry if behavior changes.
Nina Patel (Support) 2026-03-13 14:10 UTC: Noted that staggering reduced p99 by ~35% but did not eliminate spikes; escalated to runtime/allocator team.

Runtime Team (Eng) 2026-03-14 08:20 UTC: Proposed short-term patch to scheduler to honor tenant-level spread for concurrent jobs (avoid strict affinity during scheduled windows). Testing on canary pool.
SRE (Eng) 2026-03-14 11:05 UTC: Canary run shows improvement for mixed workloads; patch reduces NVLink contention on canary nodes by ~30%.
next_steps:
1) Apply scheduler spread mitigation to customer pool during next scheduled window as a targeted config (controlled rollout).
2) Add predictive headroom to autoscaler for known scheduled windows (customer-configurable).
3) Instrument more granular kernel and NVLink telemetry for dedicated pools to attribute noisy-tenant behaviour precisely.
4) Follow up with HeliosAI after two successful windows to validate fix and discuss longer-term rate-limiting/priority controls.
resolution: In Progress - Temporary mitigation applied in canary. Plan to roll targeted scheduler spread to helios-dedicated-pool-3 for next maintenance window. No permanent fix yet; engineering assigned to runtime scheduler and autoscaler teams.
